scenes.visual: Title card 'Wells Share One Scoop' over a cartoon water bottle with many wells hanging beneath it. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: BLUE = the scoop, theta (water sample holds DNA); GREEN = capture, gamma (extraction); GOLD = the well, delta (one qPCR run); FILLED TEAL pond = occupied; GREY OUTLINE pond = empty; RED dashed horizontal line = the 5% stop line. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Ponds, bottles, tubes and wells are flat labelled cartoons; bars and gauges are computed from the lesson's formula and labelled 'computed'; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: More wells cost an afternoon in the lab, not a field trip. Pond S two already gave twenty negative wells. Are those twenty tries, or only two?
scenes.caption: More wells cost an afternoon in the lab, not a field trip. Pond S2 already gave twenty negative wells. Are those twenty tries, or only two?
scenes.visual: A boot-and-bottle icon labelled 'field trip' beside a well-plate icon labelled 'afternoon in the lab'. Both slide aside; a single pond labelled 'S2' appears with a counter '20 wells: all negative'. Two tags: '20 tries?' and '2 tries?'.
scenes.narration: More wells cost an afternoon in the lab, not a field trip. Pond S2 already gave twenty negative wells. Are those twenty tries, or only two?

scenes.tts: Draw S two as a tree. The pond gives two blue water bottles. Each bottle gives two green extraction tubes. Each tube feeds five gold wells. So all twenty wells hang from just two scoops of water.
scenes.caption: Draw S2 as a tree. The pond gives two blue water bottles. Each bottle gives two green extraction tubes. Each tube feeds five gold wells. So all twenty wells hang from just two scoops of water.
scenes.visual: A tree grows downward from the pond: 2 BLUE bottles, then 2 GREEN tubes under each, then 5 GOLD wells under each tube. A counter tallies '2 bottles, 4 tubes, 20 wells'. Every well's line traces back up to one of only two blue bottles.
scenes.narration: Draw S2 as a tree. The pond gives two blue water bottles. Each bottle gives two green extraction tubes. Each tube feeds five gold wells. So all twenty wells hang from just two scoops of water.

scenes.tts: Use the workshop's numbers. A scoop holds D N A sixty percent of the time. That is theta, the blue line. The capture and well values are borrowed from a wild pig study in Texas, as illustrations only.
scenes.caption: Use the workshop's numbers. A scoop holds DNA 60% of the time. That is theta, the blue line. The capture and well values are borrowed from a wild pig study in Texas, as illustrations only.
scenes.visual: On-screen box: 'θ = 0.60 (our choice)', 'γ = 0.49, δ = 0.38 (borrowed: wild pigs, central Texas; illustrative)', 'prior = 0.20', 'stop line 5%'. Beside the tree a vertical gauge 'q: one sample's chance of detecting an occupied pond' with a BLUE horizontal line at 0.60 labelled 'θ'. Its needle sits at 0.415 (computed).
scenes.narration: Use the workshop's numbers. A scoop holds DNA 60% of the time. That is theta, the blue line. The capture and well values are borrowed from a wild pig study in Texas, as illustrations only.

scenes.tts: Try adding wells. Pour more gold wells under the same two bottles. The gauge for one sample climbs at first. Then it levels off, still below the blue line. It never crosses theta, however many wells you add.
scenes.visual: Gold wells multiply under each green tube: 5, 10, 20, 50 (counter). The q gauge needle rises from 0.415 and levels off at 0.444 (computed, two extractions per sample, unlimited wells), visibly below the BLUE θ line at 0.60. A faint dashed curve traces the plateau.
scenes.narration: Try adding wells. Pour more gold wells under the same two bottles. The gauge for one sample climbs at first. Then it levels off, still below the blue line. It never crosses theta, however many wells you add.

scenes.tts: The reason is simple. If the scoop held no D N A, every tube and every well from it is testing empty water. No number of wells can find D N A that the sample does not contain.
scenes.caption: The reason is simple. If the scoop held no DNA, every tube and every well from it is testing empty water. No number of wells can find DNA that the sample does not contain.
scenes.visual: One blue bottle is shown empty (no gold dots inside, label 'no DNA in this scoop'). Its green tubes and all its gold wells grey out together, a crossed-out icon over each. Schematic.
scenes.narration: The reason is simple. If the scoop held no DNA, every tube and every well from it is testing empty water. No number of wells can find DNA that the sample does not contain.

scenes.tts: Watch the bar for the chance that S two is still occupied. With unlimited wells on two samples, it stops at seven point two percent. That is still above the five percent line.
scenes.caption: Watch the bar for the chance that S2 is still occupied. With unlimited wells on two samples, it stops at 7.2%. That is still above the 5% line.
scenes.visual: A vertical bar 'P(S2 occupied | all negative)' beside the tree, RED dashed line at 5%. As wells keep pouring in, the bar slides from 7.9% (5 wells per tube) down to 7.2% (unlimited wells) and stops, a gap visible above the red line. Values computed.
scenes.narration: Watch the bar for the chance that S2 is still occupied. With unlimited wells on two samples, it stops at 7.2%. That is still above the 5% line.

scenes.tts: Now add a third blue bottle instead, a new scoop of water from the pond. With the usual five wells per extraction, the bar drops to four point eight percent. That is below the line.
scenes.caption: Now add a third blue bottle instead, a new scoop of water from the pond. With the usual five wells per extraction, the bar drops to 4.8%. That is below the line.
scenes.visual: The extra wells vanish. A third BLUE bottle grows from the pond with its own 2 green tubes and 10 gold wells. The bar drops to 4.8% (computed), just under the RED 5% line; a small tag 'just under' points to the gap.
scenes.narration: Now add a third blue bottle instead, a new scoop of water from the pond. With the usual five wells per extraction, the bar drops to 4.8%. That is below the line.

scenes.tts: Here is a tempting mistake. Suppose we pretend the twenty wells were twenty separate trips to the pond. Will the pond look emptier, or fuller, than the evidence allows?
scenes.visual: Back to the two-bottle tree. A dotted outline suggests redrawing each well as its own bottle. Two tags: 'emptier?' and 'fuller?'.
scenes.narration: Here is a tempting mistake. Suppose we pretend the twenty wells were twenty separate trips to the pond. Will the pond look emptier, or fuller, than the evidence allows?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; caption 'Predict: emptier or fuller?'

scenes.tts: Emptier. Redraw the tree as twenty bottles, each with one well. Each one now looks like its own try. The bar plunges to about two percent, and you would stop.
scenes.visual: The tree snaps apart into 20 separate BLUE bottles, each with one GREEN tube and one GOLD well. On screen: 'per well, as if independent: 0.60 x 0.49 x 0.38 = 0.11'. The bar plunges to 2.3% (computed), far below the RED line, tagged 'false confidence'.
scenes.narration: Emptier. Redraw the tree as twenty bottles, each with one well. Each one now looks like its own try. The bar plunges to about two percent, and you would stop.

scenes.tts: But you would stop on an error in the model, not on evidence. Counting repeated measurements of one unit as if they were separate units has a name. It is called pseudoreplication.
scenes.visual: The 20 bottles collapse back into the true tree of 2 bottles. Label across the screen: 'pseudoreplication = counting repeated measurements of one unit as separate units'. The bar returns to 7.9%.
scenes.narration: But you would stop on an error in the model, not on evidence. Counting repeated measurements of one unit as if they were separate units has a name. It is called pseudoreplication.

scenes.tts: So wells and extractions from one sample all test the same water. They are second chances at the lab steps, not new tries at the scoop. Here, adding wells cannot cross the line. A third water sample does.
scenes.visual: Side by side: left, two bottles with two extractions each and a mass of wells, gauge levelled below the BLUE θ line, bar at 7.2%; right, three bottles with five wells per tube, bar at 4.8% under the RED line. Values computed.
scenes.narration: So wells and extractions from one sample all test the same water. They are second chances at the lab steps, not new tries at the scoop. Here, adding wells cannot cross the line. A third water sample does.

scenes.visual: End card (standard Hex card), one line only: 'Only new water is a new try at the scoop.'
